newsitem.title: USA: Drug may protect pancreas during surgery - study.
newsitem.headline: Drug may protect pancreas during surgery - study.

text.p: A team of Italian doctors has identified a drug that can provide modest protection to the pancreas during surgery, according to a report in the New England Journal of Medicine.
Damage to the pancreas, which aids in digestion, is one of the most common complications of ERCP surgery, designed to examine the tubes sending fluids to the intestine from the pancreas and liver.

A team led by Dr. Giorgio Cavallini of the University of Verona found that giving the drug gabexate to 208 volunteers before surgery made them less likely to experience complications related to the pancreas, the Journal said in its Thursday edition.
While eight percent of 210 patients who received a placebo suffered an inflammation of the pancreas, the problem only surfaced in two percent of the gabexate recipients.
The results mean "gabexate reduced pancreatic damage related to ERCP," the Cavallini team said in the Journal.
It was unclear, however, how widely the drug would be accepted. ERCP is usually performed as outpatient surgery, but gabexate has to be given intravenously over a 12-hour period.

That requirement, plus its cost of about $260 per treatment, meant "the additional overall costs of gabexate therapy would be substantial," Dr. Kees Huibregtse of the Academic Medical Centre in Amsterdam said in an editorial in the Journal.
Gabexate is sold under the brand name Foy by Lepetit in Lainate, Italy, which helped pay for the study.
